title: Transition Defense Sprint Back
description: After a shot, defenders sprint back to protect the rim first and match up second, practising the priority order real transition defense demands.

content.objective: Sprint back to protect the rim before worrying about matching up to a specific player.
content.setup: A shot goes up at one end; defenders start sprinting back the instant it leaves the shooter's hand.
instructions: On the shot, all defenders sprint back toward their own basket immediately.
The first defender back protects the rim rather than chasing a specific matchup.
Remaining defenders match up to open shooters as they arrive.
Communicate 'ball', 'basket' and player numbers as the picture becomes clear.
coachingPoints: Sprint on the shot, don't wait to see if it goes in.
Protect the rim first, find a specific matchup second.
Talk the whole way back so teammates know who has whom.
commonMistakes: Jogging back and getting beaten down the floor.
Chasing a specific matchup instead of protecting the rim first.
Talking too little for teammates to react in time.
content.safety: Make sure the sprint lane back is clear of any other group.
